name: New Mexico

agency.name: New Mexico Department of Workforce Solutions, Labor Relations Division

rates2026.note: Unchanged throughout 2026; higher local rates apply in Santa Fe city and county and Las Cruces

tipped.note: State tipped cash wage since January 1, 2023; higher local tipped wages in Albuquerque ($7.20), Las Cruces ($5.20), Santa Fe County ($4.62)

minWage.other: No separate wage for students or minors.

source.quote: $12.00 per hour effective January 1, 2023 (previously $11.50 per hour effective January 1, 2022) $3.00 per hour for tipped employees effective January 1, 2023

localMinWages.name: City of Santa Fe
localMinWages.note: Living wage for all employers in city limits ($15.00 Jan-Feb 2026). Tipped workers: $3.00 base if tips bring them to $15.40. Rises to $17.50 on January 1, 2027 (ordinance passed November 2025).

source.quote: As of March 1, 2026, the Living Wage in the City of Santa Fe is $15.40 per hour , applicable to all employers within the city limits.

localMinWages.name: Santa Fe County (unincorporated)
localMinWages.note: Tipped base wage $4.62. Applies outside the City of Santa Fe, Española and Edgewood town limits.

source.quote: Current Living Wage Rates Effective March 1, 2026 Regular employees $15.40 per hour Tipped employees (base wage) $4.62 per hour
The City of Las Cruces Minimum Wage will increase on Jan. 1, 2026, from $12.65 to $13.01 an hour.

localMinWages.name: Albuquerque
localMinWages.note: City ordinance rate is $11.85 ($10.85 with qualifying health/childcare benefits), but the state's $12.00 prevails. Tipped employees: $7.20 (60% of the 2025 city minimum), higher than the state $3.00.

source.quote: Effective January 1, 2026, the City of Albuquerque minimum wage is $11.85 per hour. However, the State of New Mexico's $12.00 per hour minimum wage supersedes

overtime.note: Compensatory time instead of overtime pay is not allowed; employees cannot waive time and a half.

source.quote: state law requires overtime pay at a rate of not less than one and one-half times an employee's regular rate of pay after 40 hours of work in a week of seven days

sickLeave.accrual: 1 hour for every 30 hours worked (or 64 hours front-loaded)
sickLeave.capNote: All private employers: up to 64 hours per year (Healthy Workplaces Act).

source.quote: The Healthy Workplaces Act of 2021 is a law requiring all private employers in New Mexico to allow employees to accrue and use a benefit called earned sick leave. The law took effect on July 1, 2022

finalPay.fired: within 5 days of discharge (10 days for task, piece or commission wages)
finalPay.ptoNote: No statute requires holiday, sick or severance pay; vacation payout follows employer policy.

source.quote: If the wages owed are a fixed and definite amount, the employer shall pay such wages to the employee within five days of discharge.
Does an employer have to give lunch breaks, coffee breaks, or rest periods? No. There is no statute that requires an employer to provide such breaks

notes.text: Santa Fe's citywide living wage jumps to $17.50 an hour on January 1, 2027, then follows a formula blending inflation and local rents from 2028.

source.quote: January 1, 2027: $17.50 — a one-time legislative jump to set a more realistic baseline for Santa Fe's cost of living.

notes.text: Every private employer, regardless of size, must provide up to 64 hours of paid sick leave a year.

source.quote: The employer could choose to grant an employee 64 hours at the beginning of the year, or they can provide one hour for every thirty hours worked

notes.text: No state paid family leave program exists yet: DWS coordinated a task force whose recommendations went to the Legislature in October 2022.

source.quote: The task force will report their recommendations to the Governor and the Legislature by October 1, 2022.
